solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: That man in pub returned after this?

definitions.text: That man in pub returned after this?

indicators.note: returned asks for the whole assembled pub-with-man to be read from right to left
the man is placed inside the pub, so in signals one piece going within another

parts.note: a bar is a pub
that man is he

explanation.surface: A drinker comes back from the pub and is sent off for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes inside BAR to make BAHER, and 'returned' turns it round. The whole clue is also the definition: rehab is where a man who drank in the pub ends up afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation treatment for alcohol dependence is what a heavy pub-goer might be sent to.

clue.text: Note striking result

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
percussion is the act of striking

explanation.surface: A musical note is struck and has a lasting effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence, especially an unwelcome one, is a knock-on result.

clue.text: H from Steps essentially behind fashionable line

indicators.note: behind says the middle of Steps comes after the word for fashionable

parts.note: hot means fashionable, in demand

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the central letter, of the word Steps

explanation.surface: Someone from the pop group Steps stands behind a trendy queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like the pop group but only its middle letter E is used. HOTEL is the word for H in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio spelling alphabet each letter has a code word, and H is spoken as this one.

clue.text: Interior regulator caught unknown cheat coming back through building

indicators.note: through means the reversed run passes into the middle of the building word

parts.note: a block is a building

indicators.note: coming back asks for the three pieces before it to be read backwards

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Y is an algebraic unknown
to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: A thief is caught returning through a building's internal security system.
explanation.walkthrough: C, Y and DO read backwards give ODYC, which goes inside BLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The body's internal timer of daily rhythms is a biological regulator working inside us.

clue.text: By implication, perhaps brunette lady's cleared without justice being done

parts.note: a brunette is by implication not fair-haired, so un-fair

indicators.note: cleared means the inside of the word lady is emptied out, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dark-haired woman is acquitted though justice has not been done.
explanation.walkthrough: UN-FAIR is read as 'not blonde', so a brunette qualifies. Clearing out LADY leaves its first and last letters, LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating someone unjustly means acting with no fairness, so justice is not served.

clue.text: Reveal what one can't do in poker?

definitions.text: what one can't do in poker?

explanation.surface: A poker player wonders what they cannot reveal at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Once a poker player folds, the hand is out: there is no way to take the fold back, so 'un-fold' is impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: To open out or disclose is to reveal; in poker, folding is final and cannot be reversed.

clue.text: Maybe what McDonald's worker says to familiar Scotsman is bull?

parts.note: a fast-food server offers fries
Ian is a familiar Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A burger-bar server offers chips to a Scottish friend, and it is all nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fries, Ian?' is the server's question. 'Bull' looks like slang for nonsense, but it is a male of this black-and-white cattle breed; the question mark admits most of them are cows.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed of dairy cattle includes males, so one example of the breed is a bull.

clue.text: Bar stocking other bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A bar keeps a stock of other bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a noun for the bar's stock, but it is a verb: the words contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast block of gold or silver is a metal bar.

clue.text: What bound society to accommodate adjusted February periodically?

definitions.text: What bound society to accommodate adjusted February periodically?

indicators.note: to accommodate means the bound-and-society pair takes another piece into it

parts.note: a leap is a bound

indicators.note: adjusted says the letters picked out are put in a new order
periodically picks every other letter of the month name

explanation.surface: Society agreed to tweak February every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of February, ERAY, are rearranged to YEAR and put between LEAP and S. As a whole the clue says these years periodically fit an adjusted February.
explanation.definitionFit: Every fourth year February gains a 29th day, keeping the calendar in step with the sun.

clue.text: Processed regularly fatted goose liver, port and a pinch of seasoning

definitions.text: Processed regularly fatted goose liver, port and a pinch of seasoning

indicators.note: processed means worked over, so the letters are reworked into a new order
regularly picks every other letter running through these words
a pinch is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of seasoning

explanation.surface: A recipe for a luxury paste of fattened goose liver with port and seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters FTE, GOE, IE, PR, AD, plus A and S from seasoning, are rearranged. The whole clue also describes the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This French delicacy is a paste of fattened goose liver, often made with port and seasoning.

clue.text: Hot snooker player ultimately met people about cue manufacturer

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately picks the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A snooker star in form finally meets people who make cues.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of Hot, snooker and player (TRR) join METPEOPLE and are rearranged. 'cue manufacturer' suggests snooker cues, but this device shows a speaker their cues.
explanation.definitionFit: The autocue screen feeds a presenter lines to read, so it produces their prompts.

clue.text: Musters strength initially to pursue how to get laid?

indicators.note: to pursue means the strength letter follows the other piece

parts.note: an instruction: roll, meaning turn over, a word for call such as dial, and it reads laid

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of strength

explanation.surface: Advice on seduction tacked on to a note about physical strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how to get laid' is not about romance: rolling (reversing) DIAL, another word for 'call', gives LAID. S from 'strength initially' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Assemblies at which names are read out are musters of the troops or staff.

clue.text: Rosemary's bedfellow dated your setter

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Someone called Rosemary took the crossword setter out on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosemary' looks like a woman's name, but it is the herb; the two share a herb bed and a song line.
explanation.definitionFit: These two herbs are paired in cooking and in the folk song line with parsley and sage.

clue.text: Last item sent from Bow delivery company obtained illegally

parts.note: UPS is a parcel delivery company
hot goods are stolen

explanation.surface: The final parcel from a London district has been stolen by a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' looks like the London district, but it is an archer's bow; in archery this word is the last shot of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery the final arrow of a contest is so called, hence its usual sense of outcome.

clue.text: Street fight follows revolutionary students suffering prolonged exposure

indicators.note: follows means the fight word comes after the others
revolutionary means turning round, so the students' union letters are read backwards

parts.note: NUS is the National Union of Students
a ruck is a brawl

explanation.surface: Radical students brawl in the street after being too long in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS reversed gives SUN. NUS is Britain's National Union of Students.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected by heatstroke after too much time outdoors under strong sunshine.

clue.text: Spooner's minder arrived in Newmarket?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the first sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: a guard is a minder
came means arrived

explanation.surface: A bodyguard turns up in a Suffolk racing town.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of GUARD CAME. Newmarket looks like the horse-racing town, but it is also the name of a game played with cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Newmarket is a gambling game played with a pack, so it is one example of the type.

clue.text: This might be sprayed on dater outside party?

definitions.text: This might be sprayed on dater outside party

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go round the party word
sprayed means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone going on a date might spritz on scent before going out to a party.
explanation.walkthrough: ONDATER rearranged as DEO...RANT goes around DO. The whole clue also says what this product is for.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiperspirant or body spray is applied before a date to stop odour.

clue.text: Months playing Morse in improper term

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for month or months

indicators.note: playing suggests letters are moved about freely into another order

explanation.surface: Months spent watching the detective show Morse led to a misused word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse' looks like the TV detective, but MORSEIN is just letters to rearrange after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong or inaccurate name is an inappropriate label for something.

clue.text: Without clothing welcoming Romeo's tongue

parts.note: sans is French-derived for without

indicators.note: welcoming means the clothing word takes in the Romeo letter

parts.note: kit is clothing
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A naked man welcomes Romeo with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' suggests a kiss, but it means a language: the ancient classical one of India.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, and this is the classical language of ancient India.

clue.text: Australian killjoy impresses on retiring

parts.note: wows means impresses

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for on is read backwards

parts.note: re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: An Australian spoilsport makes a big impression on going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, meaning 'about' or 'on', reverses to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a puritanical person who disapproves of drinking and fun.

clue.text: Greatly affects uniform and plain-clothes officer arresting fence

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pen is a fenced enclosure
DS is a detective sergeant

explanation.surface: Uniformed and plain-clothes police arrest a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' looks like a receiver of stolen goods, but it is a pen, an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down is to overturn it, hence to disrupt it greatly.

clue.text: Far-out eccentric disowns The The

indicators.note: disowns means getting rid of, so the word named next is taken out

parts.note: out there means eccentric, unconventional
the band name read as the word The, the article itself

explanation.surface: A wild oddball rejects the 1980s band The The.
explanation.walkthrough: The The is an English rock band; here it means 'the word The', removed from OUT THERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre or unconventional, beyond the bounds of normal taste.

clue.text: What bow and arrow do to supply with money

parts.note: both words finish with the same pair of letters, so the phrase says they end in those letters

explanation.surface: An archer's gear asked to fund someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow and arrow both END in OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone an income or a fund is to provide them with money.

clue.text: Number for Spice Girl making a comeback: That's All Right

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: making a comeback means the singer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Mel B is one of the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl's comeback single is a cover of an Elvis hit.
explanation.walkthrough: MEL B reversed gives BLEM. 'That's All Right' looks like a song title, but it is a casual reassurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is fine and causes no difficulty is a casual reassurance.

clue.text: Inane lackey in government primarily making false statements

indicators.note: inane means empty, so the lackey word loses its middle
primarily takes the first letter of government

explanation.surface: A brainless servant in government is telling lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Empty LACKEY of its inside to leave LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling untruths is the act of uttering falsehoods.

clue.text: Orthodox US woman books top celebrities behind play

indicators.note: behind means the woman and other pieces come after the play word

parts.note: fun is play
dame is American slang for a woman
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: An American woman reserves top stars for a stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' looks like reserves, but it gives NT, the New Testament. DAME is American slang for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict adherent to traditional religious doctrine is rigidly orthodox.

clue.text: Up charges against broadcaster

indicators.note: against means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Sky is a British broadcaster
wards are people in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A broadcaster brings charges against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like accusations, but it means young people in someone's care. Sky is a British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading upward toward the heavens is moving up.

clue.text: Row about golf that could become ferocious

indicators.note: about means the row word goes around the golf letter

parts.note: a tier is a row
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A row over golf might turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The wild cat is a creature that could turn ferocious.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cat is an animal that may turn savage when provoked.
